experiments.conditions: Full-scale 10-ft propeller ahead of a liquid-cooled engine nacelle (Curtiss Conqueror, geared 7:5), NACA 20-ft open-throat propeller-research tunnel, V up to ~115 mph (51 m/s); blade angles 15-45 deg at 0.75R (pitch_deg = angle - 15); rpm per row from the report schedule; thrust is EFFECTIVE thrust (shaft tension minus slipstream increment of nacelle drag); no tunnel-wall correction stated (open throat 20 ft, prop 10 ft).
experiments.source: Hartman & Biermann 1938, NACA Report 640, Fig. 13 (C_T, p. 8) and Fig. 15 (C_P, p. 9) (digitised)
experiments.uncertainty: digitising ct +-0.0015, cp +-0.003, J +-0.005; repeat tests within ~1 % (report p. 3)

sources.citation: Hartman, E.P., Biermann, D.: The aerodynamic characteristics of full-scale propellers having 2, 3, and 4 blades of Clark Y and R.A.F. 6 airfoil sections. NACA Report No. 640, 1938.

Deters, R.W., Ananda, G.K., Selig, M.S.: Reynolds number effects on the performance of small-scale propellers. AIAA 2014-2151 (NR640 = scaled 5868-9), and UIUC Propeller Data Site vol. 2, NR640 design geometry files nr640_geom.txt / nr640_thick.txt
Biermann, D., Hartman, E.P.: The effect of compressibility on eight full-scale propellers operating in the take-off and climbing range. NACA Report 639, 1938 (tip-speed effects on these data).

notes: Geometry digitised from R-640 Fig. 2 and cross-checked against the UIUC NR640 design table (agreement within 1 % chord, 0.1 deg beta). twist_deg = blade angle beta from the plane of rotation at the 15 deg setting (beta(0.75R) = 15 deg exactly); pitch_deg in the experiment = (blade angle at 0.75R) - 15, so a 30 deg test has pitch_deg = 15. Rhub = 0.2R = first tabulated station (blade shank, modelled as a cylinder with cd 1.0 to r/R 0.25, transition at 0.30); the propeller runs in front of a large nacelle (43 x 38 in, i.e. ~0.30-0.36 of D), no spinner, so the inner ~0.3R sits in the nacelle blockage - the measured thrust is EFFECTIVE thrust (minus slipstream drag increment on the nacelle) and eta is propulsive efficiency of the propeller-nacelle unit, both a little below isolated-propeller values. Airfoils: Clark Y family generated by y-scaling the UIUC Clark Y; polars are XFOIL (Ncrit 9, incompressible), no measured section data used (measured Clark Y: NACA TR 502 Silverstein, 11.7 % only, Re up to 8.6e6). Reynolds number at 0.75R ~1.2e6-2.0e6. COMPRESSIBILITY: tip speeds 600-1200 rpm -> helical tip Mach 0.29-0.6 (column tip_mach); the 2-blade 15/20 deg runs at 1200 rpm reach M_tip ~0.57-0.6 - per NACA TR 639 these coefficients are slightly lowered in the take-off range; the polars are incompressible, so add a Prandtl-Glauert correction if the solver has one. Low-J take-off parts of the charts are drawn dashed (faired/extrapolated) and are excluded. The report states the tabulated test points were only available on request (not published), so the faired chart curves are the data.
